messages:
maya: heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC refactor we started seeing control-plane rejects for a few on-prem customers. error shows up during control-plane handshake: `403: principal not allowed by vpc_allowlist`.

jon: can you paste the exact log and the role mapping you rolled out?

maya: paste below. this is from private-controlplane logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T18:02:11Z ERROR auth: authz failed principal="user:svc-account:acme-team" reason="not in vpc_allowlist"
2026-03-17T18:02:11Z DEBUG rbac: matched_role=pcp-superuser mapped_groups=["pcp:admins"]
```
and here's the mapping we shipped: `roles.yaml` snippet:
```
- role: pcp-superuser
  binds: ["group:pcp:admins", "group:pcp:operators"]
  principals: ["svc-account:*", "user:*@acme.com"]
```

olivia: quick theory: vpc_allowlist check runs after principal->group translation, but our new role names use `pcp:` prefix while allowlist entries are plain AWS-principal ARNs. if the control-plane is constructing an allowlist key with `pcp:` prefix it won't match. did we change the principal normalization?

maya: i thought normalization was unchanged. i grepped the rollout branch and found this commit that adds `pcp:` prefix to group names during mapping: https://git.internal/redwood/pcp/commit/ab12cd (edge-case change from the refactor). that likely breaks the string comparison we use for allowlist keys.

luis: if that's true, workaround is to add the mapped principal pattern to the customer's allowlist (eventual fix to normalization). can we patch the mapping to emit raw principals instead? quick patch idea: strip `pcp:` when computing allowlist lookup. example: `allow_key = principal.replace(/^pcp:/, '')`.

jon: i don't love mutating strings at lookup time. better: make allowlist check canonicalize both sides (strip prefixes) and add a migration to normalize stored allowlist entries. short-term patch: add a compatibility check to allow both prefixed and unprefixed forms.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by maya for branch `pcp/allowlist-compat` — canary to 3 customers in us-west after approval.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0417-07 — 3 customers affected, severity P2. automated rollback is disabled for this change.

olivia: also noticed KMS integration check failing for one on-prem site: key policy rejects `pcp-superuser` role when using assumed-role flow. probably separate but related: roles gain new name and KMS key policy matched on old role name. KMS policies tend to be exact-match.

luis: for KMS, best short-term: update key policy to include the new `pcp-superuser` ARN alongside existing. longer-term: update our role-name migration doc and add a script to patch key policies for private deployments.

maya: i've drafted a minimal PR (link: https://git.internal/redwood/pcp/pull/432) that implements allowlist compatibility and adds a one-off migration script `scripts/normalize-allowlist.sh` that prints the delta. can reviewers + security please ack? cc @jon @olivia

jon: reviewing now. also add unit tests for canonicalization logic and an integration test hitting a mock control plane with prefixed/unprefixed inputs.

olivia: agreed. also open a follow-up ticket to update onboarding docs for private customers on how role names map to KMS policies and VPC allowlists — customers should not need to change anything during refactors.

luis: ran the migration in staging and confirmed it would add 2 entries for the effected customers. staging logs:
```
apply-migration: customer=acme add_allowlist_entries=["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/pcp-superuser", "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/superuser"]
```

maya: patch merged and canary deployed to the 3 affected customers. monitoring shows failed handshakes dropped to 0 for those tenants. will keep canary for 24h, then full rollout.

jon: once canary stabilizes, please follow up with a short postmortem: root cause = role-name prefix introduced by refactor + strict string matching in allowlist/KMS policies. remediation = allowlist canonicalization, key-policy patch, migration script, docs. add mitigation ideas: e2e test with role-name fuzzing.

maya: noted. created PM ticket PM-778 and linked PR/incident. thanks all. :thumbsup:

luis: one last note — if you touch control-plane allowlist code, add a debug flag to log canonicalized principals (safe-scrubbed) so we can catch this earlier next time.

deploy-bot: canary completed successfully for customers: acme, beta-inc, delta-ops. rollout scheduled to remaining private deployments in 2h.

sre-bot: INC-2026-0417-07 severity downgraded to P3 and will be closed after postmortem attached.

maya: closing thread when postmortem attached.
